sourcedFrom: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip out of Staccato's own XL instructions: slide stop out, slide forward off the frame, then the Dawson Precision tool-less guide rod captured on its own takedown lever and turned clear of the link before the barrel comes out the front. No bushing wrench and no plug wrestle — the captured rod is what makes this different from a plain 1911.

steps.title: Gun clear, workspace clear of ammunition
steps.action: Before anything moves, confirm the pistol is clear and get the loose ammunition off the bench. Staccato asks for the workspace itself, not just the gun — a round left on the mat is how a stripped pistol gets loaded again by accident on reassembly.
steps.quote: Ensure your gun is clear, and your workspace is free of ammunition.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Racked, and checked in both chamber and magwell
steps.action: Pointed somewhere safe, rack the slide to the rear and look into the chamber and the magazine well — both. A check of one place only is how a round left in the other gets missed.
steps.quote: With the pistol pointed in a safe direction, rack the slide to the rear and visually inspect the chamber and magazine well to make sure the pistol is empty.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Takedown notch lined up with the slide stop knuckle
steps.action: Draw the slide back — not to lock, but to where the takedown notch in the slide sits over the knuckle of the slide stop — and hold it there. If the notch is not aligned the slide stop will not start out, and forcing it is how the frame gets scarred.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to line up to take down notch on the slide with the slide stop knuckle.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 3

steps.title: Slide stop pushed through from the opposite side and removed
steps.action: Push on the end of the slide stop pin from the other side of the pistol with a fingertip or a small tool, and draw the slide stop out. It should move under light pressure — if it fights you, the slide has drifted off the notch.
steps.quote: Push on the slide stop pin from the opposite side of the pistol using a finger or a small tool and remove the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 4

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the top end gently forward off the frame rails and set the frame down. Keep it level as it comes — tipping it lets the recoil assembly start to move inside the slide before it has been captured.
steps.quote: Gently pull the slide forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Flange pushed forward to expose the tool-less rod's takedown lever
steps.action: Push forward on the flange of the guide rod. That compresses the spring far enough to bring the takedown lever on the Dawson Precision tool-less rod into reach. Keep your thumb on the flange — the spring is now under load.
steps.quote: Remove the Dawson Precision® Tool-Less Guide Rod, by pushing forward on the flange of the guide rod to expose the takedown lever.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 6

steps.title: Lever lowered onto the reverse plug, system out rotated clear of the link
steps.action: Depress the lever and lower it onto the reverse plug — that captures the recoil system as one unit. Then take the captured assembly out from the shooter's side, turning it as it comes so its notch clears the barrel link. This is where the XL differs from the Staccato P: it comes out with a rotation, not straight out the back.
steps.caution: The spring is compressed and held only by that lever on the plug. An uncaptured tool-less rod under load will launch — do not let the flange slip forward while you are seating the lever.
steps.quote: Depress the lever and lower it down onto the reverse plug to capture the system and pull it out from the shooter side of the screen tool, rotating it so that the notch can clear the link.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 7

steps.title: Link forward, barrel out of the muzzle end
steps.action: Slide the link forward along the barrel so it clears, then draw the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide. That completes the strip — frame, slide stop, slide, captured recoil assembly and barrel. Staccato's written procedure goes no further than this.
steps.quote: Slide the link forward on your barrel and pull it out from the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, step 8

steps.title: Rails, frame surfaces and feed ramp brushed and wiped
steps.action: With a brush and a rag or paper towel, clear the debris off the slide rails, the frame surfaces and the barrel's feed ramp.
steps.prose: The feed ramp is the one most often skipped. Carbon there is where feeding trouble starts, and the rails carry the grit the slide rides on every shot.
steps.quote: Use a brush and a cleaning rag or paper towel to clear away debris from the slide rails, frame surfaces, and barrel feed ramp.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: Bore brushed breech to muzzle, then oiled and wiped back out
steps.action: Run the bore brush through the barrel from breech to muzzle, as many times as it takes. Then put a small amount of CLP on a bore mop and oil the bore, and wipe the excess back out with a clean patch.
steps.prose: Breech to muzzle pushes the fouling out the front instead of back into the chamber. The clean patch at the end is the point — a film of oil in the bore, not a wet one.
steps.quote: Use your bore brush to clean the bore of the barrel, from breech to muzzle. And repeat this process as needed.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

steps.title: A few drops on the slide rails and barrel contact points
steps.action: Put a few drops of lubricant on the slide rails and on the barrel's contact points, and no more.
steps.prose: Staccato says a few drops. More than that does not make the pistol run better — it holds powder residue and grit where the slide and barrel move.
steps.quote: Apply a few drops of lubricant to your slide rails and barrel contact points.
steps.cite: Staccato XL Disassembly — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series — Disassembly, cleaning

deepAbsentReason: The page ends at the field strip. Staccato's XL article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato XL', and its written steps stop at the frame, slide stop, slide, captured recoil assembly and barrel, followed by cleaning and reassembly. No extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip-module procedure is published on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. For anything else the page directs owners to contact Staccato's Customer Service directly. Nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: RAILS, FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush and wipe debris off the slide rails
Brush and wipe the frame surfaces

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore brush from breech to muzzle, repeated as needed
A small amount of CLP on a bore mop to oil the bore
A clean patch to wipe the excess oil back out

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A few drops on the slide rails
A few drops on the barrel contact points

reassembly: Check the link is flipped forward toward the muzzle, then reinstall the barrel.
Rotate the guide rod into place, push on the rear of the flange to release the takedown lever, and lower it gently against the barrel.

Line the slide rails up with the frame rails and run the slide on. Staccato's own note: the guide rod flange must be pushed up against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must not be rotated to either side, or the top end will not slide fully onto the lower.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the slide stop's pin must pass through the link's hole or the pistol will not function. If it is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the knuckle of the slide stop, then seat the slide stop fully into the frame.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery and that the slide stop is fully seated in the frame — Staccato's own last step is to rack the slide to check for proper function. Anything that does not run as it should goes to Staccato's Customer Service, not back into service.
